summary: Scripts demonstrate solid bash knowledge (set -euo pipefail, quoting, error handling) and workflow structure is sound. Critical issues: (1) aggregate-test-results.sh uses jq (lines 82-92) to parse JSON but workflow never installs it—relies on ubuntu-latest having jq pre-installed, violating explicit-dependencies best practice; (2) run_act_tests.sh uses act-ubuntu-pwsh:latest image tag (line 36) instead of pinned version; (3) no runtime jq availability check before attempting JSON parsing. XML parsing via awk is intentionally simplistic and fragile. Undeclared jq dependency makes maintainability difficult. Would not ship without explicit jq installation in aggregate job and version pinning.
